name: Supply & installation
summary: Equipment selection, delivery and installation for AUX, CLIVET or dehumidifier projects, each quoted on its own.
intro: Cosmix Engineering supplies and installs HVACR equipment for commercial, institutional and industrial buildings. The brand on the project stays the brand in the quotation: an AUX system, a CLIVET system, or a dehumidifier is not bundled into one mixed schedule.
points: Help matching a building to a series in the relevant catalogue
Delivery coordination to the Karachi or Lahore office, or to site
Installation planned around the building’s ceiling, plant room and power supply
Handover with the operating settings agreed for that project
applies: Offices, hotels, hospitals, malls, campuses and industrial buildings are the kinds of projects named in the company’s own material.

name: Operation & maintenance
summary: Inspections and repairs that keep an installed system in service and limit unplanned stoppages.
intro: Once a system is running, Cosmix offers operation and maintenance: regular inspections, preventive care and repairs. The aim is straightforward — fewer breakdowns, and equipment that keeps the conditions it was installed for.
points: Scheduled inspection of the installed plant
Repairs arranged through the same team that knows the project
Attention to filters, drains, controls and the outdoor or plant-room units
A record of what was found, so the next visit starts from a known condition
applies: Maintenance is quoted for the equipment already on site. AUX, CLIVET and dehumidifier plant are discussed separately.

name: General electro-mechanical
summary: Electro-mechanical work that sits beside the air-conditioning plant: power, installation and upgrades.
intro: The company describes a broader electro-mechanical service around the HVACR work: installations and upgrades that support the plant, with an emphasis on safety and on keeping the building’s systems reliable.
points: Installation work associated with HVACR equipment
Upgrades where an existing system has to be changed rather than replaced in full
Coordination with the building’s electrical supply and the equipment’s requirements
Site work from the Karachi head office and the Lahore office
applies: Scope is agreed per building. This page is not a product catalogue.

name: Testing, balancing & adjustment
summary: Measuring and adjusting air and water systems so they deliver what the design asked for.
intro: Testing, balancing and adjustment (TBA) is the work of measuring a finished system and tuning it. Cosmix offers TBA so airflow, water flow and controls are brought into line with the way the building is meant to run.
points: Airside measurements on ducted and packaged systems
Waterside checks where the project uses chillers and fan coils or air handlers
Adjustment of terminals, dampers and controls after installation
A clear note of the readings taken on that visit
applies: TBA is most useful just after installation and again when a building’s use changes.

name: Energy audit
summary: A look at how the HVACR plant uses energy, and which changes are worth making.
intro: An energy audit from Cosmix looks at the installed heating, cooling and ventilation plant and points out where energy is being wasted. The result is a set of practical recommendations, not a generic certificate.
points: Review of operating hours, set-points and the equipment actually installed
Notes on maintenance issues that are also wasting energy
Recommendations ranked by what they change on this building
A written summary the facilities team can act on
applies: Audits are scoped to the plant on site. The company does not publish a named certification for this service.

name: Ducting
summary: Duct design and installation so air from the indoor unit or air handler reaches the rooms.
intro: Ducting is part of how a concealed or packaged system serves a building. Cosmix designs and installs ductwork to suit the equipment and the rooms, so air arrives where it is needed and the unit is not fighting the duct run.
points: Duct routes planned around the ceiling void and the equipment’s static pressure
Installation coordinated with the indoor units, air handlers or rooftop packages
Grilles and access arranged so the system can be balanced and cleaned
Work quoted with the equipment brand it serves, not as a mixed package
applies: Typical places are offices, shops, hotels and any building using ducted indoor units or a central air handler.
